event.description:
We invite you to join the Des Moines Art Center in welcoming artist Alison Saar as the featured speaker of our annual Fingerman Lecture series. Saar’s work examines the place of the female body in the realms of politics and spirituality. She explores Black female identity, and the powerful, multifaceted roles women play — from everyday life to timeless, legendary figures.

Saar has exhibited artworks at many galleries and museums throughout the United States. Her art is represented in the collections of the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Baltimore Art Museum, the Museum of Modern Art, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Her 1997 piece, “Sweeping Beauty” was added to the Des Moines Art Center’s permanent collection in 2003.

event.description:
Welcome to Fright Night at the Art Center! The Des Moines Community Playhouse’s Final Act Ensemble brings ghosts, witches, murder, and mystery to life in a Halloween performance inspired by the golden age of radio.

The evening features three chilling tales: “The Woman Who Wouldn’t Die,” in which a man begins to suspect his wife may be a witch burned more than 200 years ago; a spooky story of stranded teenagers, a possible dead body, and a mysterious stranger; and “The Moonlit Road,” Ambrose Bierce’s classic tale about a man who discovers the terrifying truth behind his mother’s murder.

For nearly 20 years, the Final Act Ensemble—a company of older adult actors—has performed polished old-time radio shows throughout the Des Moines area. This production features live acting, music, and sound effects.

Free; no registration required. Run time: approximately 50 minutes.

Please note: This program may not be suitable for younger children. The stories include death, murder, supernatural themes, eerie music, and spooky sound effects. Although portions of the performance are humorous, some children may find the program frightening.

event.title: “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way” Curator and Artist Discussion
event.venue_json: {"id":2590,"global_id":"desmoinesartcenter.org?id=2590","venue":"Levitt Auditorium","address":"4700 Grand Ave","city":"Des Moines","country":"United States","state":"IA","zip":"50312","url":"https://desmoinesartcenter.org/venue/levitt-auditorium/","show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
Join the Des Moines Art Center for an invigorating discussion about the traveling exhibition organized by the Buffalo AKG Art Museum, “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way: Contemporary Latinx Painting,” which is on view at the Art Center from October 24, 2026, through January 24, 2027. Inspired by a 2008 poem of the same name by former US Poet Laureate Juan Felipe Herrera, “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way” celebrates the vision and creativity of Latinx painters. It showcases 58 artists who actively enrich the landscape of contemporary painting, introducing new approaches to form, materials, and subject matter.

Dr. Andrea Alvarez, curator of the exhibition, will provide insight into the premise of the show and introduce us to three of the featured artists: Danielle De Jesus, Justin Favela, and Patrick Martinez.

REGISTER

Danielle De Jesus is a Nuyorican painter and photographer born and raised in Bushwick, Brooklyn, whose woks tell the story of growing up in New York City amid gentrification and displacement. De Jesus’s background is in photography, and she utilizes her images of people native to Bushwick as a reference to tell the story of the community’s displaced residents.

Justin Favela is based in Las Vegas and is known for large-scale installations and sculpture that manifest his interactions with American pop culture and the queer Latinx experience. Favela explores traditional Mexican and Latin American craft — specifically cartoneria (a traditional Mexican folk art form that involves three-dimensional objects using papier-mâché and cardboard) — and his interest in art history, community, celebration, and home inform a practice intent on dismantling institutional hierarchies. Visitors may remember Favela from his 2021 exhibition at the Art Center, “Central American.”

Patrick Martinez maintains a diverse practice that includes mixed-media landscape paintings, neon signs pieces, cake paintings, and his Pee Chee series of appropriative works. His landscape paintings composed of Los Angeles surfaces — distressed stucco, spray paint, window security bars, vinyl signage, ceramic tile, and neon sign elements — evoke place and socioeconomic positions, unearth sites of personal and cultural loss. He lives and works in Los Angeles.

Free; registration required.

REGISTER

Image: Top left: Andrea Alvarez, curator of the exhibition. Artists in the exhibition; top right:  Patrick Martinez, bottom left: Justin Favela, and bottom right: Danielle De Jesus.

event.title: Day of the Dead / Día de Los Muertos
event.venue_json: {"id":1642,"global_id":"desmoinesartcenter.org?id=1642","venue":"Des Moines Art Center","address":"4700 Grand Ave","city":"Des Moines","country":"United States","state":"IA","zip":"50312","url":"https://desmoinesartcenter.org/venue/des-moines-art-center/","show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
Day of the Dead 2026: ¡Sí Se Puede!

Join us for the 26th annual Día de los Muertos at the Des Moines Art Center—our largest community celebration of the year. Rooted in Mexican tradition, Día de los Muertos is a time to gather in remembrance, honoring loved ones who have died through joy, ritual, storytelling, food, art, and shared celebration. The Art Center is pleased to help create space for this meaningful community tradition each year.

This year’s theme centers on civil rights, inspired by the phrase ¡Sí Se Puede! (“Yes, we can”), created by Dolores Huerta for the United Farm Workers movement. Together, we honor the people and collective efforts that have strengthened Latino communities in Iowa and across the United States, while reflecting on the power of gathering, shared purpose, and community care.

Visitors will enjoy live music and dance performances, food and art vendors, hands-on art activities, a festive Catrina photo opportunity, a community ofrenda, and a short documentary film featuring this year’s honoree, Felicia Timotea Leon Mullin. Free hot cocoa and samples of pan de muerto will be available while supplies last, and a complimentary shuttle will run from Merrill Middle School for easy parking.

Inspired in part by the Art Center’s current exhibition “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way: Contemporary Latinx Painting,” this year’s event reflects gathering, belonging, and the ways communities care for one another. In partnership with Progress Iowa and other community organizations, we’ll also recognize local leadership and the collective work of building stronger communities.

Acompáñanos a celebrar la vigésima sexta (26ta) edición anual del Día de los muertos en el Des Moines Art Center: nuestra festividad comunitaria más popular y predilecta del año. Con raíces en la tradición mexicana, el Día de los Muertos es un momento para reunirnos en conmemoración, rindiendo homenaje a nuestros seres queridos fallecidos a través de la alegría, los rituales, las narrativas, la comida, el arte y la celebración en comunidad. Para el Art Center es un honor ayudar a crear un espacio para esta importante tradición comunitaria cada año.

La temática de este año explora los derechos civiles, inspirada por la frase ¡Sí Se Puede!, creada por Dolores Huerta para el movimiento de la Unión de Campesinos (United Farm Workers). Juntos, honramos a las personas y los esfuerzos colectivos que han fortalecido a las comunidades latinas en Iowa y en todo Estados Unidos, reflexionando también en torno al poder de la concurrencia, un propósito común y el cariño por la comunidad.

Habrá música y presentaciones de baile en vivo para disfrutar, vendedores de comida y arte, actividades interactivas de arte, oportunidades para tomarse fotos festivas con el personaje de la Catrina, una ofrenda comunitaria y un breve documental en reconocimiento a Felicia Timotea Leon Mullin, la homenajeada de este año. Habrá chocolate caliente y pan de muerto gratis hasta agotarse la existencia; también tendremos transporte gratuito desde la escuela Merrill Middle School para estacionar con facilidad.

Inspirado, en parte, por la exhibición concurrente del Art Center, Reunámonos de manera esplendorosa (Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way), el evento de este año hará reflexión respecto a la concurrencia, la pertenencia y las maneras en que las comunidades demuestran cariño y se preocupan unas por otras. En colaboración con Progress Iowa y otras organizaciones comunitarias, también reconoceremos a líderes locales y su trabajo colectivo en la construcción de comunidades más fuertes.

En esencia, el Día de los Muertos en el Art Center se trata de nuestra comunidad. Es un espacio donde el arte, la cultura, los recuerdos y la tradición compartida unen a las personas. El Des Moines Art Center se enorgullece de ser un espacio cultural de bienvenida e inspiración para todas las personas.

event.description:
Join the Des Moines Art Center for an exploration of what it means to honor the spirit — of loved ones, of cultural traditions, and of movements that have advanced justice and strengthened our communities.

At the center of the conversation is this year’s Day of the Dead ofrenda, created by poet and artist Michaela Mullin, in honor of her mother, Felicia Leon Mullin, and alongside local organizations which are continuing to advance the quality of life for all Iowans. Through the ofrenda and this year’s theme, Sí Se Puede!, panelists will consider how we remember those who have contributed to civil and human rights work, how their values live on through the people and communities they influenced, and why this work remains urgent today.

Opening with a brief Know Your Rights presentation led by Karina Sanchez of the Des Moines Civil and Human Rights Commission, this program will feature a conversation with Mullin; Vince Valdez, historian, filmmaker, and longstanding Day of the Dead committee member; and Erica Johnson, the founding Executive Director of Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice. Art Center Senior Manager of Museum Learning and Engagement, Mia Buch, will moderate. Join us for an inspiring conversation about remembrance, immigrant rights, community action, and carrying the work of previous generations forward.

Free; no registration required.

event.description:
The ReelAbilities Film Festival is the largest festival in the US dedicated to promoting awareness and appreciation of the lives, stories, and artistic expressions of people with disabilities. Founded in New York City in 2007, the festival presents international and award-winning films by and about people with disabilities in multiple locations throughout each hosting city. The 2026 Des Moines festival, “A Taste of ReelAbilities,” is a screening of recent short films during the Art Center’s November Social Saturday: Friendsgiving. All films will provide open captions and have audio description capabilities.

Generous support provided by Art Bridges Foundation’s Access for All program.

Free; no registration required.

Screening Information:
Film: A Morning with Aroha, 2021
Director: Nicholas Rini
Run Time: 11 minutes
Description: Aroha, an imaginative young girl with Down syndrome, sets out to share her creativity with her neighbors.

Film: Key of Genius, 2026
Director: Daniel Persitz
Run Time: 12 minutes
Description: Based on the extraordinary true story of Derek Paravicini, a blind, autistic musical prodigy, KEY OF GENIUS follows the bond between Derek and his dedicated piano teacher. Through patience, intuition, and unwavering belief, Derek’s hidden potential is unlocked, revealing the transformative power of music and mentorship. This film celebrates talent, perseverance, and the ways people with disabilities can flourish when given opportunity and understanding. Audiences are invited into a journey of inspiration, emotional depth, and triumph, witnessing a remarkable story of human connection, creativity, and the extraordinary capabilities that lie within those societies often underestimated.

*The following films are intended for adult audiences.

Film: Boys, 2026
Director: Olive Bilic
Run Time: 7 minutes
Description: Overwhelmed by the chaos of class, neurodiverse teenager Jacob seeks refuge in an empty locker room, only to face an unexpected confrontation. Created in collaboration with Bus Stop Films participants in Melbourne, BOYS highlights the emotional and social challenges faced by neurodiverse youth. Through authentic performances and an intimate lens, the film portrays the tension, vulnerability, and resilience of its characters, exploring the fine line between isolation and connection. BOYS is both a poignant and engaging narrative, offering insight into neurodiverse experiences while emphasizing the universal desire for understanding, acceptance, and human connection.

Film: Little Monsters, 2026
Director: Pablo Leridon
Run Time: 14 minutes
Description: A visually impaired teen navigates first love while sharing a transport van with a wheelchair-bound classmate. LITTLE MONSTERS blends humor and heart, showcasing adolescence, rivalry, and inclusive friendship.

Film: Bad Survivor, 2026
Director: Alex Dvorak and Katie North
Run Time: 11 minutes
Description: After being “broken up with” by her oncologists, a sarcastic young cancer patient begins her first day in remission, navigating the challenges of returning home. With humor and biting honesty, she confronts her family dynamics, cultural expectations, and the lingering trauma of treatment. BAD SURVIVOR balances comedy and pathos, portraying survival not as a singular triumph but as a process filled with awkward moments, personal reflection, and familial tension. Audiences are drawn into an intimate portrait of post-cancer life, where resilience, wit, and emotional vulnerability coexist, redefining what it means to move forward after illness.

Film: Don’t Take this the Wrong Way, 2026
Director: Rachel Handler and Crystal Arnette
Run Time: 7 minutes
Description: Darcy, beaten down by microaggressions and a recent breakup, begins to unravel emotionally. DON’T TAKE THIS THE WRONG WAY presents a raw exploration of personal vulnerability, societal pressures, and coping with isolation. The short captures moments of introspection, tension, and resilience, offering audiences an intimate glimpse into the lived experience of an amputee navigating social and emotional challenges. Through concise storytelling and authentic performances, the film conveys the complexity of identity, self-esteem, and the subtle ways everyday interactions can shape one’s emotional landscape.

Film: Misfit, 2026
Director: Tristan Zerbib
Run Time: 13 minutes
Description: In a world where disability is the norm, wheelchair-ball dominates the sports scene. A player is thrown off balance when forced to train with a ‘valid’ athlete, challenging her expectations and assumptions. MISFIT turns conventional sports narratives upside down, celebrating empowerment, inclusion, and the unpredictability of competition. Through fast-paced action and engaging character work, the film explores societal perceptions of ability and the courage required to embrace difference. MISFIT is a bold, energetic story that champions physical resilience, adaptability, and teamwork while entertaining audiences with humor, tension, and the triumph of spirit.

Film: Rearranged, 2025
Director: Liz Whitmere
Run Time: 12 minutes
Description: Set within the intimate confines of a hospice, REARRANGED explores how irritation, vulnerability, and humor can unexpectedly give way to human connection. Led by blind actor Bruce Horak, the film challenges assumptions about care, agency, and intimacy, revealing how small disruptions can reshape relationships.

Film: Them That’s Not, 2025
Director: Mekhai Lee
Run Time: 19 minutes
Description: Andrea “Drea” Stoney, a Deaf poet, attends her grandmother’s repass and navigates a family that doesn’t understand ASL. Complicating matters, her father is temporarily released from prison for the day, forcing Drea to reconcile with him amid grief. THEM THAT’S NOT explores identity, communication, and familial tension, highlighting the challenges Deaf individuals face within hearing-centered spaces. Through introspection, subtle humor, and emotional honesty, the film portrays the resilience required to carve personal space and connection, offering audiences insight into Deaf culture, intergenerational dynamics, and the quiet power of language, love, and understanding.
